short_title: Les Mills vs City Fitness Value
title: Les Mills vs City Fitness NZ — Which Is Better Value in 2026?
meta_desc: Compare Les Mills and City Fitness NZ in 2026: pricing, contracts, facilities, class quality and city coverage to find the best gym value for Kiwi members.
intro: Kiwi gym‑goers are hunting the best bang for their buck. In 2026 Les Mills and City Fitness sit at opposite ends of the price‑contract spectrum – let’s see which delivers true value.

sections.heading: Contract Terms & Commitment
sections.body: Les Mills requires a 12‑month minimum with an automatic renewal clause; early exit incurs a $100 break‑fee. City Fitness operates on a pure month‑to‑month basis, no joining fee, and a 14‑day cancellation window.

sections.heading: Facilities & Equipment
list: Indoor pools – Wellington City Fitness only
Sauna & steam rooms – Les Mills Auckland clubs
Kids’ drop‑in area – City Fitness Auckland locations

sections.heading: Group Fitness Class Quality
sections.body: Both brands run the full Les Mills programme (BODYPUMP, RPM, BODYCOMBAT, etc.). Les Mills clubs hire instructors with an average of 5+ years experience and offer smaller class sizes (max 20). City Fitness uses a mixed‑model: Les Mills classes plus in‑house formats, but classes can reach 30 participants, leading to a slightly diluted experience.

sections.heading: Cities Covered
sections.body: Les Mills operates clubs in Auckland (Mount Eden, Ponsonby), Hamilton, Wellington, and Christchurch. City Fitness has a larger footprint in Auckland (Mt Eden, New Lynn, Manukau, Westgate) and also in Wellington; a Christchurch site is slated for early 2027.

sections.heading: Which Offers Better Value?
sections.body: If you prefer a low‑cost entry point and no long‑term commitment, City Fitness wins on flexibility. For members who value premium facilities, smaller class sizes and a proven Les Mills instructor base, Les Mills delivers higher per‑dollar quality despite the contract.
